slides.title: SwapBot: Tool-Centric Robot Manipulation via Interchangeable End-Effectors and Tactile Sensing
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that integrating tactile sensing into modular, swappable end-effectors significantly improves imitation learning performance for contact-rich manipulation tasks, offering a practical pathway for robust skill acquisition in tool-centric environments.

card.one_liner: SwapBot enables tool-centric manipulation via low-cost adapters, tactile sensing, and imitation learning.
card.key_idea: Modular system converts household tools into robot end-effectors with integrated tactile sensors and fast autonomous swapping.
card.evaluation: User studies and real-world cooking tasks show tactile feedback boosts imitation learning success by 15-25% over RGB-only.
card.limitation: Tactile sensors are low-resolution and prone to wear; policy learning relies on predefined task segmentation.

slides.title: Kinematic-Tactile Aligned Dexterous Retargeting with Contact Wrench Space Alignment
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that aligns both kinematics and tactile contact wrenches when retargeting human demonstrations to robot hands, significantly improving replay success rates in contact-rich tasks like pouring.

card.one_liner: A retargeting framework aligning human kinematics and tactile wrench spaces for dexterous robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Hierarchical three-stage method using object-centric contact wrench space to align kinematics, contact geometry, and tactile forces.
card.evaluation: Tested on real robot pouring tasks with varying payloads; achieved 96.7% success rate and higher wrench fidelity than baselines.
card.limitation: Requires synchronized tactile and kinematic data; relies on quasi-static assumptions and specific contact geometry for force conversion.

slides.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: TouchBridge demonstrates that tactile-conditioned retargeting can effectively transfer contact-rich human demonstrations to robots without physics simulation, offering a scalable approach to skill acquisition that aligns with MOSAIC's focus on integrating procedural skill data from human demonstrations.

card.one_liner: TouchBridge enables scalable human-to-robot transfer for dexterous manipulation using tactile-conditioned retargeting.
card.key_idea: Hardware-software framework aligning visual/tactile sensing; Tac-Retarget preserves contact patches via optimization without object meshes or simulation.
card.evaluation: Four real-world tasks; 72.5% success vs 77.5% teleoperation; 7x faster collection; outperforms DexPilot/UniDex by 25-42.5 points.
card.limitation: Validated on modest dataset size; requires specific hardware alignment and may need scaling to diverse human data.

slides.title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
slides.highlight: Vision-language-action policies frequently initiate movement and complete unintended tasks even when given empty or nonsensical instructions, revealing a critical safety gap in autonomous robot behavior.

card.one_liner: VLA policies start moving without instructions, requiring action-difference gates for safe suppression.
card.key_idea: Paired protocol tests VLA start behavior under empty/invalid instructions; gate suppresses start if action chunks match empty-input output.
card.evaluation: Six LIBERO-Goal checkpoints tested on 200 states; gate achieved 98-100% non-start on non-task inputs with minimal success loss.
card.limitation: Instruction prefixes failed; fine-tuning unreliable; gate requires two inference calls and may miss infeasible task-specific instructions.

slides.title: Direct Action-Manifold Modeling for Efficient and Robust Bimanual Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces a single-step action generation method that reduces latency and improves robustness in bimanual manipulation, addressing execution mismatch issues relevant to real-time hybrid human-AI team coordination.

card.one_liner: DMAT enables single-step bimanual action generation via direct manifold modeling, outperforming diffusion baselines in speed and robustness.
card.key_idea: Reformulates action generation as direct clean chunk prediction from stochastic interpolants, using local 3D geometry and spectral-time refinement for state consistency.
card.evaluation: Tested on Fourier GR2 robot across 567 trials (standard/OOD/intervention), showing higher success and 2x faster inference than IDP3 and DiTFlow3D baselines.
card.limitation: Relies on specific conditional action-manifold hypothesis and complex heuristic STR parameters, potentially limiting generalizability to tasks with unstructured action spaces.

slides.title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
slides.tldr: OBJECT-CENTRIC SKILL LEARNING FROM EGOCENTRIC VIDEOS
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates how object-centric reinforcement learning from egocentric videos can decouple skills from specific hand trajectories, offering a method to improve the transfer of human-like dexterous manipulation relevant to MOSAIC's goal of aligning human and AI intent through skill acquisition.

card.one_liner: HandMimicX learns generalizable dexterous manipulation skills from single egocentric videos via object-centric RL.
card.key_idea: Object-centric RL framework using depth-refined HOI reconstruction and interaction priors to decouple skills from specific hand trajectories.
card.evaluation: 8 simulation tasks (85.4% avg success) and real-world UR5/Wuji hand tests (71.3% success), outperforming SimToolReal and Dex4D.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate 3D reconstruction; limited to discrete contact regions without force modeling; narrow embodiment scope.

slides.title: Nexus-VLA: Bridging Human and Robot Experiences via a Shared Hierarchical Semantic Latent Space
slides.highlight: Nexus-VLA aligns human and robot manipulation experiences through a shared hierarchical semantic latent space, enabling direct knowledge transfer from egocentric human videos to robot policies. This approach addresses embodiment gaps in visual appearance and kinematics, offering a method for integrating human procedural knowledge into robot action learning.

card.one_liner: Nexus-VLA bridges human-robot gaps via a shared hierarchical semantic latent for end-to-end policy learning.
card.key_idea: Jointly trains on unpaired human/robot data using a unified latent encoding multi-level semantics (intent to interaction) for direct action generation.
card.evaluation: Tested on RoboCasa-GR1 (80.5% success), OOD settings, and real robots; outperforms baselines like ACE-Ego-0 and GR00T-N1.6.
card.limitation: Relies on offline structured experts for semantic supervision; real-world gains depend on high-quality human video data availability.

slides.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that observation and action representations, rather than optimizer settings, are the primary determinants of real-world success in dexterous manipulation, while showing that offline metrics cannot fully replace physical robot evaluation.

card.one_liner: Real-robot ablations show representation choices dominate imitation learning success, while offline metrics only partially predict performance.
card.key_idea: Systematic real-robot ablations of 281 policies reveal that observation/action representations (e.g., ROI cropping, robot-base frames) outweigh optimizer or sampling choices.
card.evaluation: 1,700 real-robot trials on RJ45 insertion; 67 offline metrics tested, with only motion smoothness correlating with success within specific policy families.
card.limitation: Offline metrics fail to generalize across policy families or predict grasp success, necessitating expensive real-robot evaluation for reliable selection.
